name: Hertz contact theory
domain: 车辆—轨道与基础结构动力学
definition_zh: 依据弹性接触变形计算接触法向力的理论。
usage_note: 本文法向力计算采用非线性Hertz关系，不能代替切向蠕滑力模型。
usage_overview: 常用于车辆—轨道耦合分析，由轮轨法向弹性压缩确定非线性法向接触力，也用作接触模型的比较基准。在满足局部曲率等假设的接触计算中，可用于求解椭圆接触斑，并作为条带计算的基础；其法向接触关系不能代替切向蠕滑力模型。

complete_examples.text: In this example, it is assumed a train grouped by three identical four-axle vehicles runs with a constant velocity of 300 km per hour on a simply-supported 3 span bridge, as shown in Fig. 2, and comparisons are conducted to illustrate the accurateness of the proposed model in characterizing the system dynamic behaviours and wheel/rail interactions, in which the conventional solutions, as references, are respectively derived by the models of Zhai et al. [17], Hertz contact theory and FastSim program by Kalker [28].
In the hybrid model, the nonlinear Hertz contact theory is used, while in this model, wheel–rail rigid contact model is applied to improve the computational stability and efficiency.

Furthermore, based on the study of Wang (1984) and Yan and Wang (1985), Zhai (1996, 2004) proposed the calculation method of wheel–rail geometric relationship, introduced the Hertz contact theory and Kalker creep theory, established a three-dimensional vehicle–track coupled dynamics model, which is the basic theoretical framework of vehicle–track coupled dynamics (Zhai, 2015).

The wheel-rail contact is simulated by introducing the Hertz contact theory, where the transient contact stiffness of wheel-rail impacts is calculated by Kr = (G Δz)3/2 Δz ̃x (8) where G is the Hertzian contact constant; Δz denotes the relative displacement between the wheel and rail.
The coupling of the vehicle system and track system [35] is implemented by the wheel-rail inter action involving nonlinear Hertz contact theory and Kalker creep theory.

The well-known nonlinear Hertz contact theory and Kalker’s linear creep theory with nonlinear modifications have been introduced in the wheel–rail coupled dynamic model [39] with refined description of the contact geometry and nonlinear characterization of the contact forces in normal and tangential directions.
The coupling of wheel and rail is described by the nonlinear Hertz contact theory [25] and Kalker linear creep theory [26], respectively.
